knowledge_point.title: Identifying True Statements Using the Invertible Matrix Theorem and the Rank-Nullity Theorem

question.:question/problem:
Which of the following statements are true given that $A$ is a $10\times 10$ matrix with $0$ pivot columns?

I. $\text{rank}(A)=5$

II. $A$ is invertible

III. $\text{nullity}(A)=10$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $A$ is a $10\times 10$ matrix, the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

$A$ is invertible $\,⇔\,\left\{\begin{aligned}\text{Col}(A) &={R}^{10} \\ \text{dim(Col}(A)) &=10=\text{rank}(A) \\ \text{Null}(A) &=\{0\} \\ \text{dim(Null}(A)) &=0=\text{nullity}(A)\end{aligned}\right.$

Also, according to the rank-nullity theorem, if $A$ is a matrix with $n$ columns, then 

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

The 0 pivot columns give $\text{rank}(A)=0.$

By the rank-nullity theorem,

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n,\qquad 0+10=10.
$$

Hence $\text{rank}(A)=0$ and $\text{nullity}(A)=10$. Since rank is less than the number of columns, $A$ is not invertible and $\det(A)=0$. Also, $\text{Col}(A)$ has dimension 0, there are 0 pivot columns, and there are 10 non-pivot columns.

- Statement I is false.

- Statement II is false.

- Statement III is true.

Therefore, the correct answer is III only.

question.:question/problem:
Which of the following statements are true given that $A$ is a $21\times 21$ matrix which has only $2$ non-pivot column?

Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $A$ is a $21\times 21$ matrix, the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

$$
A\text{ is }\text{invertible}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\left\{\begin{aligned}\operatorname{Col}(A) &=\mathbb{R}^{21} \\ \dim(\operatorname{Col}(A)) &=21=\operatorname{rank}(A) \\ \operatorname{Null}(A) &=\{0\} \\ \dim(\operatorname{Null}(A)) &=0=\operatorname{nullity}(A)\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Also, according to the rank-nullity theorem, if $A$ is a matrix with $n$ columns, then 

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

The 2 non-pivot columns give $\text{nullity}(A)=2.$

By the rank-nullity theorem,

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n,\qquad 19+2=21.
$$

Hence $\text{rank}(A)=19$ and $\text{nullity}(A)=2$. Since rank is less than the number of columns, $A$ is not invertible and $\det(A)=0$. Also, $\text{Col}(A)$ has dimension 19, there are 19 pivot columns, and there are 2 non-pivot columns.

- Statement “$A$ is invertible” is false.

- Statement “$\text{Col}(A)$ is a $19$-dimensional subspace of ${R}^{21}.$” is true.

- Statement “$\text{nullity}(A)=9$” is false.

Therefore, the correct answer is $\text{Col}(A)$ is a $19$-dimensional subspace of ${R}^{21}.$.

question.:question/problem:
Which of the following statements are true, given that $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and  $\text{Null}(A)=\left\{\begin{bmatrix}2a \\ a \\ b\end{bmatrix}\,|\,a,b\in R\right\}?$

Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix, the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

$$
A\text{ is }\text{invertible}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\left\{\begin{aligned}\operatorname{Col}(A) &=\mathbb{R}^{3} \\ \dim(\operatorname{Col}(A)) &=3=\operatorname{rank}(A) \\ \operatorname{Null}(A) &=\{0\} \\ \dim(\operatorname{Null}(A)) &=0=\operatorname{nullity}(A)\end{aligned}\right.
$$  

Also, according to the rank-nullity theorem, if $A$ is a matrix with $n$ columns, then 

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

The supplied null space has the independent spanning vectors

$$
\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix},\;\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}
$$

Thus $\text{nullity}(A)=2.$

By the rank-nullity theorem,

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n,\qquad 1+2=3.
$$

Hence $\text{rank}(A)=1$ and $\text{nullity}(A)=2$. Since rank is less than the number of columns, $A$ is not invertible and $\det(A)=0$. Also, $\text{Col}(A)$ has dimension 1, there are 1 pivot columns, and there are 2 non-pivot columns.

- Statement “$A$ is not invertible” is true.

- Statement “$\text{rank}(A)=1$” is true.

- Statement “$det(A)=0$” is true.

Therefore, the correct answer is $A$ is not invertible; $\text{rank}(A)=1$; $det(A)=0$.
